children.text: Magnetic levitation

A small spherical permanent magnet can be treated as a point dipole m=q_mδm, represented by south and north magnetic charges −qm,+qm with displacement δm from south to north. The north pole defines its position. A monopole produces \(\mathbf B=\mu_0q_m\hat r/(4\pi r^2)\) and experiences force qmB. Write B=−∇Φ. A uniform conducting film extends infinitely in xy, occupies −d≤z≤0, has conductivity σ, and lies height h below the source, with h≫d. Neglect displacement current and take induced volume current uniform across d. In A a north monopole appears at (0,0,h) at t=0 and remains there. Neglect propagation delay. Initially its image above the film calculation is +qm at (0,0,−h), and below-film calculation uses −qm at the real source position. The supplied film equation is ∂²B′z/∂z²=μ0σ∂B′z/∂t after neglecting lateral derivatives in the thin-film approximation. In B a source moves along +x at fixed h for its whole prior history and is at x=0 now. In C take a type-I superconductor with σ→∞ and a horizontally fixed dipole m x̂ of mass M0 in gravity −g ẑ. Ignore orientation coupling and air damping.

Find total B(ρ,z) at t=0 for z≥0 away from the monopole.

Find the initial total field for z≤−d.

Find initial magnetic flux through either film surface.
a.4. Induced current density
Find the initial induced volume current j(ρ) using the thin-film approximation.
a.5. First-order surface evolution
Integrate the film equation across thickness to obtain a first-order equation near z≈0.
a.6. Surface evolution solution
Find the general form of B′z near the surface for t>0.
a.7. Receding image speed
Show the induced field represents a downward-moving image and find its speed.
b.1. Hopping-source images
Approximate motion by hops vτ at times −nτ,n≥0. Each hop creates +qm at the new position and −qm at the old. Give present image positions for both types.
b.2. Image monopole potential
Write and evaluate the image-potential sum Φ+(x,z) in the y=0 plane as τ tends to zero.
b.3. Lift and drag on a vertical dipole

nodes.alt: Original vertical dipole travelling horizontally above the conducting film.

children.text: The moving dipole has fixed moment m ẑ. Find its force at the present position (0,0,h).
b.4. Copper image speed
For σ=\(5.9\times10^{7}\) Ω⁻¹m⁻¹,d=0.50 cm,h=5.0 cm calculate v0.
b.5. Skin-depth correction
The skin depth is δ=√[2/(ωμ0σ)] with ω=max(v,v0)/h. Estimate v0(v) in low- and high-speed regimes, replacing film thickness by skin depth if smaller.
b.6. Crossover speed
Find vc where the low- and high-speed estimates meet.
c.1. Superconducting equilibrium height
Find h0 for the horizontal dipole of mass M0.
c.2. Vertical oscillation frequency
Find angular frequency Ω of small vertical oscillations.
c.3. Micromagnet height
A sphere has R=1.0 μm,ρ0=7400 kg/m³,magnetization M=0.75 T/μ0 and g=9.8 m/s². Calculate h0.
c.4. Micromagnet oscillations
Calculate Ω for that sphere.

children.text: Magnetic levitation
a.1. Initial field above the film

Sum the real and positive image fields: \[\mathbf B=\frac{\mu_0q_m}{4\pi}\left[\frac{\boldsymbol\rho+(z-h)\hat z}{(\rho^2+(z-h)^2)^{3/2}}+\frac{\boldsymbol\rho+(z+h)\hat z}{(\rho^2+(z+h)^2)^{3/2}}\right].\]
a.2. Initial field below the film
The negative image at the source cancels its field in the lower region, so B=0.
a.3. Initial surface flux

At z=0 the two normal components cancel pointwise, and below the film the field vanishes. The total flux through any patch of either surface is zero. The source writes B′z=0 in one explanation, but it is the total Bz that vanishes, not the image contribution by itself.
a.4. Induced current density

Ampère's law across the film gives \(\mathbf j=(\hat z\times\mathbf B_{above})/(\mu_0d)\). Thus \[\mathbf j=\frac{q_m}{2\pi d}\frac{\hat z\times\boldsymbol\rho}{(h^2+\rho^2)^{3/2}}.\] The current is azimuthal and produces the opposing initial normal field.
a.5. First-order surface evolution

The induced normal field is even about the midplane, so its derivatives at opposite faces are opposite. Neglect variation of its time derivative across d. Integration gives \(2\partial_zB_z^{\prime}=\mu_0\sigma d\,\partial_tB_z^{\prime}\), or \(\partial_tB_z^{\prime}=v_0\partial_zB_z^{\prime}\), with v0=2/(μ0σd).
a.6. Surface evolution solution
The characteristic solution is \(B_z^{\prime}(\rho,z;t)=f(\rho,z+v_0t)\), with f determined by the initial induced field.
a.7. Receding image speed
The initial image field depends on z+h. Replacing z by z+v0t places the image at zimage=−h−v0t. Thus the downward speed is \(v_0=2/(\mu_0\sigma d)\).
b.1. Hopping-source images
Positive images are at \((-nv\tau,0,-h-nv_0\tau)\). Negative images are at \((-(n+1)v\tau,0,-h-nv_0\tau)\). Their differing lateral positions retain the history of motion.
b.2. Image monopole potential

Put H=z+h. The sum is \[\Phi_+=\frac{\mu_0q_m}{4\pi}\sum_{n\ge0}\left[\frac1{\sqrt{(x+nv\tau)^2+(H+nv_0\tau)^2}}-\frac1{\sqrt{(x+(n+1)v\tau)^2+(H+nv_0\tau)^2}}\right].\] Its continuum limit is \(\mu_0q_mv/(4\pi)\int_0^\infty(x+vt)[(x+vt)^2+(H+v_0t)^2]^{-3/2}dt\). Evaluation gives \[\Phi_+=\frac{\mu_0q_mv}{4\pi(Hv-v_0x)}\left[\frac H{\sqrt{x^2+H^2}}-\frac{v_0}{\sqrt{v^2+v_0^2}}\right].\] At a removable zero of the denominator use the integral or its continuous limit.
b.3. Lift and drag on a vertical dipole

Form the image-dipole potential \(\Phi_T=\delta_m\partial_z\Phi_+\), differentiate for the field, then take the north-minus-south force while holding the image source fixed during field differentiation. This yields \[F_z=\frac{3\mu_0m^2}{32\pi h^4}\left(1-\frac{v_0}{\sqrt{v^2+v_0^2}}\right),\quad F_x=-\frac{v_0}{v}F_z,\quad F_y=0.\] Lift is positive and drag negative for v>0. Both vanish continuously as v tends to zero.
b.4. Copper image speed
\(v_0=2/(\mu_0\sigma d)\simeq5.4\,\mathrm{m/s}\).
b.5. Skin-depth correction

At low v the skin depth exceeds d, so v0(v)=2/(μ0σd), the B4 constant. At high v, δ<d and ω≈v/h, so \[v_0(v)=\frac2{\mu_0\sigma\delta}=\sqrt{\frac{2v}{\mu_0\sigma h}}=\sqrt{v_0dv/h}.\] This is an effective-thickness estimate beyond the uniform-through-thickness low-speed model.
b.6. Crossover speed
Set δ=d with ω=vc/h: \(v_c=2h/(\mu_0\sigma d^2)=v_0h/d\). For the copper dimensions it is about 54 m/s.
c.1. Superconducting equilibrium height

For a perfect diamagnetic plane the horizontal image has the same horizontal moment at z=−h. Its repulsive force is \(F_z=3\mu_0m^2/(64\pi h^4)\). Balance M0g to obtain \[h_0=[3\mu_0m^2/(64\pi M_0g)]^{1/4}.\]
c.2. Vertical oscillation frequency
The derivative of the magnetic force at h0 is −4M0g/h0. Thus \(\Omega=\sqrt{4g/h_0}\). This is angular frequency in rad/s.
c.3. Micromagnet height
Use m=(4πR³/3)M and M0=(4πR³/3)ρ0. Then \(h_0=[\mu_0M^2R^3/(16\rho_0g)]^{1/4}\simeq25\,\mathrm{\mu m}\).
c.4. Micromagnet oscillations

Using h0≈25 μm, \(\Omega\simeq1.25\times10^3\,\mathrm{rad/s}\), or f≈200 Hz. The source loosely labels the angular frequency in kHz and substitutes a rounded 30 μm in one line. Angular frequency and cycles per second are distinguished here.
